report.summary: The single failing test, test_current_year_is_accepted, is a test bug: it posts a book with year THIS_YEAR + 1 and expects 201, but the app correctly rejects any year above the current year with 422. Fix the test to use THIS_YEAR (the name says 'current year') rather than changing the app, since the same file's test_invalid_book_is_rejected expects next-year to be rejected.

causes.title: Test submits next year and expects it to be accepted
causes.explanation: The test is named test_current_year_is_accepted but passes year=THIS_YEAR + 1. The application validates years against the current calendar year (1 <= year <= today.year), so a future year is rejected with 422, which is the intended behavior. The test file itself contradicts the test: the parametrized test_invalid_book_is_rejected case 'next-year' asserts that THIS_YEAR + 1 returns 422 'Year must be between'. The test's expectation is the wrong one; the boundary it is meant to check is the current year itself, so the input should be THIS_YEAR. This is deterministic, not timing-dependent, so it fails every run.
evidence: tests/api/test_books_api.py:47-48: def test_current_year_is_accepted(api): response = api.create_book(title=unique("New"), author="Someone", year=THIS_YEAR + 1)
tests/api/test_books_api.py:58: ({"title": "T", "author": "A", "year": THIS_YEAR + 1}, "Year must be between"), with ids 'next-year' expecting 422
app/main.py:81-84: if book.year is not None: this_year = date.today().year; if not 1 <= book.year <= this_year: raise HTTPException(422, f"Year must be between 1 and {this_year}")
causes.suggested_fix: In tests/api/test_books_api.py, change test_current_year_is_accepted to use year=THIS_YEAR (not THIS_YEAR + 1) so it checks the current-year boundary is accepted. Keep the next-year case in test_invalid_book_is_rejected as it is. No application change is needed.
